newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares rise, gains seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares rise, gains seen limited.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.08 percent on Wednesday pushed up by fresh investor optimism but traders doubted the rally had sufficient momentum to last beyond this week.

"It seems some optimism returned to the market but although there could be further gains to the end of this week, it is hard to say that today's rise is the beginning of a positive trend," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.
The SBI index closed 14.19 points up at 1,325.11. Traders noted, however, that turnover remained relatively low at 134.2 million schillings after 77.2 million on Tuesday.
"The income of fresh foreign capital is in the air. Each large domestic purchase fuels the questions: are foreigners behind it?" said Predrag Stamenkovic, of brokerage BPH.
Foreign money has held off since February when the central bank ordered international investors to open special custodian accounts. The first accounts are expected in mid-May.
Mineral water producer and health resort operator Radenska was the top gainer, jumping 6.1 percent to 1,817 tolars on volume of 3,240 shares for total turnover of 5.9 million tolars.
"Radenska was underpriced. Regarding its business performance and future outlook it should definitely have a higher price -- I expect it to stabilize around 1,900 tolars," said Stamenkovic.

Aroma producer Etol was the most actively traded share and the day's leading decliner, falling 1.67 percent to 17,199 tolars on volume of 2,279 shares for total turnover of 39.2 million tolars. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
